design.data_generating_process: continuous Gaussian trait with species baseline linked to geographic centre plus a centered quadratic local-position effect whose curvature sign is reversed in the specified fraction of species

comparators: naive pooled pairwise Spearman on geographic distance vs absolute trait difference
equal-species matched-null omnibus of within-species distance-trait rho

interpretation.supported: Under a shared quadratic within-species response, the correctly specified common quadratic model is substantially more powerful than direction-invariant distance-dissimilarity inference, while a common linear slope has little power. When half the species reverse curvature sign, the common quadratic coefficient cancels and loses power, whereas the distance-dissimilarity matched-null statistic retains substantial power because it targets strength of spatial trait organization rather than a shared curvature sign. Method performance follows estimand alignment rather than a universal ranking.
not_supported: matched-null inference is always more powerful than nonlinear models
a common quadratic model is inappropriate when species share curvature direction
the observed maximum null rejection fractions from 40 worlds are universal type-I error rates
a maximum matched-null null rejection fraction of 0.075 in one 40-world cell demonstrates systematic anti-conservative calibration
absolute pairwise trait difference is optimal for every nonlinear phenotype
the benchmark covers arbitrary nonlinear functions, multivariate traits or MNAR observation processes
